sentences.text: Lee Yuan Siong remains Executive Director, Group Chief Executive and President, and led the 2026 interim results briefing with Group CFO Garth Jones and regional chief executives Jacky Chan, Fisher Zhang, Hak Leh Tan and Leo Grepin.

In February 2026 AIA appointed Ben Ng as Group Chief Risk Officer and named Shulamite Khoo and Ku Man (David Ku) independent non-executive directors from 5 February 2026; Jack Chak-Kwong So retired as an independent director at the 22 May 2026 AGM, and Lee relinquished the chairman, director and CEO roles at subsidiary AIA Co between May and June 2026.

mgmt_team_view.text: Lee Yuan Siong has led AIA as group chief executive and president since June 2020, having previously been an executive director and co-CEO of Ping An Insurance and, before that, a senior executive at Prudential plc. AIA reported record 2025 results, with value of new business up 15 per cent to US$5,516 million and operating profit after tax up 12 per cent per share, and said it was confident of meeting or exceeding its 9 to 11 per cent OPAT per share growth target for 2023 to 2026. Embedded value equity rose 14 per cent per share to US$79.7 billion after returning US$4.7 billion to shareholders, while the shareholder capital ratio was 221 per cent, down from 236 per cent largely because of those returns.

thesis_pillars.text: AIA Group Limited is the largest independent publicly listed pan-Asian life insurance group, with a presence in 18 markets. In the first half of 2026 value of new business reached a record US$3,212 million, up 10 per cent, with annualised operating ROEV of 18.0 per cent and operating profit after tax up 13 per cent per share, leading AIA to expect it will exceed its 9 to 11 per cent OPAT per share growth target for 2023 to 2026. Capital returns are substantial, with US$3.6 billion paid out through dividends and buy-backs in the half and the interim dividend raised 10 per cent. High private savings, ageing populations and low insurance penetration remain structural demand drivers in Asia.
